function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity as a natural phenomenon had been noticed since antiquity—e.g., the Greeks observed static sparks from amber—but the first systematic scientific study of it was carried out by **William Gilbert** (1544‑1603). He coined the word *electricus* (from Latin *electrum*, meaning amber) and distinguished between magnetism and electrostatics. Later experiments by scientists such as **Benjamin Franklin**, **Alessandro Volta**, and **Michael Faraday** built on Gilbert’s work and laid the foundations of modern electrical science.
